models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light NW-quadrant airs and near-flat seas over the islands now - but the 4 Oct start is 13 days out and entirely beyond any model horizon.
briefing.synopsis: No organised pressure feature is showing over the Aeolians: the consensus across ECMWF IFS (20 Sep 00Z), ECMWF AIFS (20 Sep 06Z) and ICON-2i (20 Sep 00Z) is 2-8 kt, mostly from the NW through N, with a brief overnight backing to SW at Portorosa. Through 22 Sep the models nudge the flow to W-NW and a touch stronger, 6-8 kt with gusts to 15-18 kt around midday. MFWAM and ECMWF WAM (both 20 Sep 00/06Z) keep total wave height between 0.08 m and 0.38 m everywhere, swell 0.04-0.34 m. The forecast data ends at 23:00 on 26 Sep, so nothing here speaks to the trip dates at all.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: For tonight, 20 Sep, the rehearsal berth is Portorosa Marina - enclosed, all-round shelter, and with 1.9-3.9 kt at Portorosa through the day (IFS/AIFS consensus) the choice does not matter. Nothing in the payload would push a boat to move. Treat this as a dry run: the real fleet is not on the water yet.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: 21 Sep looks benign at Portorosa: 4.6 kt from SW at 06:00, seas 0.10 m. The rehearsal Portorosa to Lipari leg scores 'go' with a 06:00 departure and about 5 kt on a close reach. Note one disagreement around midday - the models span 3.7 to 10.3 kt at Portorosa at 12:00, so do not plan on the 6.7 kt mean as a given.

passage_notes.note: Rehearsal verdict go, 06:00 start, ~5 kt close reach. Rehearsal only - no data exists for 4 Oct.
Go, ~8 kt broad reach. At Panarea, Drautto is the recommended buoy field; San Pietro takes 12 kt ENE straight in.
Go, ~8.8 kt close hauled. Marina del Gabbiano scores 'workable' only - it is open from every direction.
Go, ~2 kt. Gusts to 13 kt are an interval-maximum in near-calm air, reported not flagged.
Go, ~9.9 kt head to wind - motor. Rehearsal shows deterioration after 10:00, so an early start scored better.
Go, ~8.1 kt on the nose; gusts to 23 kt against an 8 kt mean, single-model interval maximum. Deteriorates after 11:00. This is the end of the data - 26 Sep 23:00.

cautions: The trip dates (4-8 Oct) are 13 days out and the data ends 26 Sep. Nothing in this briefing forecasts the trip; expect the picture to be meaningless until roughly 7 days before departure.

Where 'models_range_kt' appears - Salina 20 Sep 06:00 (1.7-10.9 kt), Portorosa 21 Sep 12:00 (3.7-10.3 kt), Lipari/Panarea/Stromboli 22 Sep 18:00 (1.8-9.3 kt) - the models genuinely disagree and the mean should not be quoted as certain.

IFS and ICON-2i gusts are interval maxima, so gust factors of 3-4x over a 2-5 kt mean (e.g. 21.0 kt at Panarea on 20 Sep 06:00) look alarming but are not a squall signal. AIFS publishes no gust field.
briefing.confidence_note: Wind-speed stability is good - mean run-to-run shifts of 0.6-1.1 kt out to 120 h - but direction shifts average 48-62 deg at short lead in these light airs, and the trip dates themselves are wholly outside the forecast horizon.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
